title: Marketing Webinar Campaign Sync
next_steps: Redwood to share speaker slide deck and two-slide product overview by 2025-06-12
Nimbus to confirm final speaker bios and headshots by 2025-06-13
Set up event page in HubSpot and share link for review by 2025-06-14
Schedule technical dry-run (30m) w/ presenters on 2025-06-24
action_items: Alex Chen: Share Redwood slide deck and short speaker notes; due 2025-06-12
Elena Torres: Send final speaker bios + headshots; due 2025-06-13
Samir Gupta: Create initial HubSpot event page and UTM plan; due 2025-06-14
Priya Patel: Confirm webinar platform (Zoom vs ON24) and send tech checklist; due 2025-06-12
summary: Planning sync for joint webinar targeting data platform and ML engineering audiences. Discussed dates, goals (registrations and pipeline), promotional channels, technical runbook, UTM/tracking, and handoff for leads. Agreed on content flow, responsibilities, and next steps including assets and dry-run date.
transcript:
Header: Date: 2025-06-10 09:30 PT | Duration: 49m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Rivera (Redwood CSM), Jordan Lee (Nimbus Marketing Manager), Samir Gupta (Nimbus Demand Gen), Elena Torres (Nimbus Events)

Summary: Quick planning sync to align on webinar date, goals, promotional plan, and asset handoffs.

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll keep this to about 45 minutes, quick agenda is date, audience, promo plan, tech and next steps. Jordan you mentioned you had a couple of date constraints?
[00:18] Jordan: yeah thanks Alex, um we're aiming for end of June or first week of July but we do have a product launch week the week of July 7 that we want to avoid, so June 25-26 or July 9 looks best, but we prefer June 26 if that works for Redwood.
[00:33] Priya: June 26 should be fine on our side, let me check capacity for the SE to present, I think Priya can lead the demo portion, oh sorry that's me, yeah I can run the demo.
[00:45] Samir: for lead goals we're thinking 400 registrants and 80–100 attendees live, with a 5–7 SQL target in the following 30 days. Is that in line with your expectations?
[00:58] Alex: that's reasonable; for a co-hosted webinar with paid support we can probably hit those numbers — what budget are you thinking for paid?
[01:07] Samir: initial plan is $3k paid on LinkedIn plus $1k on retargeting display via DemandHub, but we can be flexible. We do want to prioritize LinkedIn and organic emails to our existing list.
[01:19] Maya: one quick ask, Redwood, can you provide a two-slide product overview that we can use in the invite and social copy? A short blurb for the landing page would be great too.
[01:29] Alex: absolutely, I'll share a 2-slide overview and a 60–90 word blurb. We'll also include a couple quick customer quote snippets if you want.
[01:38] Jordan: helpful — also on audience, we want to target ML platform leads, infra engineers, and developer tooling folks — not broad marketing. So the messaging needs to be technical but approachable.
[01:48] Priya: perfect, we'll tailor the demo and talking points to highlight latency/cost tradeoffs, dedicated capacity, and private deployments — but avoid deep infra jargon. We'll prepare a 10–12 minute demo and an architecture slide showing routing/caching at a high level.
[02:05] Elena: on logistics — platform wise we usually use Zoom webinars, but we've been trialing ON24 for richer analytics. Any preferences from Redwood?
[02:15] Priya: Zoom is simplest; ON24 gives more engagement metrics but has a steeper integration. If Nimbus plans to run more enterprise webinars ON24 could be worth it, but for this first co-hosted run I'd recommend Zoom to reduce friction.
[02:29] Jordan: ok let's go Zoom for now then. Elena will set it up and share the join link.
[02:35] Samir: tracking question — can Redwood provide UTM suggestions and a recommendation for converting attendees to MQLs? We use HubSpot and need a consistent UTM schema.
[02:45] Alex: yes, we'll share a recommended UTM plan and a sample HubSpot form config. Also we can send a follow-up email template for nurtures and a suggested lead scoring threshold for SQL conversion.
[02:59] Jordan: great. Also we want to do a couple of promotional bursts: 2 emails to our list, 3 social posts, and 2 paid LinkedIn pushes. Redwood do you have an institutional social post we can co-brand?
[03:12] Alex: we'll provide co-branded social tiles and two copy variants — one technical, one higher-level. We'll also share a graphic for the landing page.
[03:23] Elena: timeline wise, when do we need the assets? We need to publish the event page by Monday next week to hit our cadence.
[03:31] Alex: we can get slides and blurb by Thursday, that gives you Fri-Mon to build the page — is that ok?
[03:38] Jordan: yes that works if we get the assets by Thursday.
[03:42] Priya: tech checklist items: test presenter mics, ensure screen sharing works for demo, stage a mini load test for recorded demo content so playback isn't laggy, and confirm the panelist roles in Zoom (panelist vs attendee). Also confirm we aren't sharing any sensitive customer data in the demo.
[03:58] Samir: we'll make sure the demo data is sanitized; can Redwood supply a redwood-safe demo dataset or instructions to mask PII?
[04:07] Priya: yes we have a sanitized script and a small dataset we can provide. I'll attach that in the follow-up.
[04:14] Maya: for registration form fields we usually capture company, title, number of employees, and two qual questions — do you recommend any Redwood-specific fields?
[04:23] Alex: company and title are most important, maybe add a checkbox for "interested in dedicated deployments" yes/no, that helps routing. Also an optional field for "primary cloud provider" could be useful.
[04:35] Jordan: good idea. We'll add those.
[04:38] Elena: rehearsal plan — can we do a 30-minute run-through a week before? Prefer Tuesday the week of the event.
[04:46] Alex: yes let's schedule a 30m dry-run; propose 2025-06-19 for rehearsal and a final tech check 2 days before the event.
[04:55] Jordan: sounds good.
[04:57] Samir: reporting — how will leads be handed off? We use HubSpot; Elena wants to export a list and import, but ideally Redwood posts registrant metadata to HubSpot too.
[05:08] Maya: for enterprise campaigns we can set up a webhook to push registrants and attendees into a shared workspace; otherwise we can do CSV export. For this run, what's easiest for Nimbus?
[05:18] Jordan: CSV import is fine but if Redwood can push leads directly to HubSpot via integration that would save us time.
[05:26] Alex: we can support a simple CSV and also set up a HubSpot integration if you want us to in time — that may require some config and a security review though.
[05:37] Samir: one more question on branding — do you have a Redwood logo in SVG and a short legal blurb for the footer we can use?
[05:44] Alex: yes we'll provide logo assets and a 2-line legal blurb.
[05:49] Priya: on content flow, proposed agenda: 5m intro, 10m Nimbus use-case, 12m Redwood demo, 15m architecture and Q&A, 7–10m wrap and CTA. That should be 50–55 minutes but we can tighten.
[06:06] Jordan: prefer 45–50 max; maybe cut architecture to 10 and leave Q&A 15.
[06:13] Alex: ok we'll aim for 45 total with 12 demo + 10 tech + 15 QA plus short intros.
[06:21] Elena: any compliance or legal notes — do we need an MoU or co-host agreement?
[06:27] Maya: not usually for marketing co-hosts but we should share a short co-marketing agreement covering logos, use of assets, and lead ownership; I can draft a one-pager.
[06:36] Jordan: perfect.
[06:38] Samir: are there any competitors we should avoid mentioning? We sometimes call out BrightTALK or ON24 but not by name.
[06:46] Alex: we'll avoid direct competitor calls in slides, keep it neutral.
[06:50] Priya: final note on analytics: we'll ensure the landing page includes UTMs and a hidden field for campaign id so both teams can reconcile.
[06:58] Alex: great. recap of next steps: Redwood sends slides + blurb by Thu (6/12), Priya to send demo dataset and tech checklist, Nimbus builds HubSpot event page and shares link by 6/14, schedule dry-run 6/19, final tech check 6/24, and actual webinar target date 2025-06-26.
[07:18] Jordan: thanks all, we'll lock the date and circulate calendar invites.
[07:21] Alex: thanks everyone, talk soon.

End of transcript.
